matches.gold_text: Proposals must be received by the City by 3:00 p.m. PT on September 17, 2024.
Proposals must not be submitted by fax.
The vendor must offer ERP software and services that satisfy all of the City's functional and technical requirements.
The preferred vendor has experience successfully implementing the proposed solutions for cities of similar size and scope of services.
Any best-of-breed Human Capital Management solution offered must be able to integrate with the selected ERP system.
A vendor responding with a best-of-breed solution must complete the Section 6 Requirements template for the relevant functionality and submit it per the Section 5 instructions.
The vendor must provide an integrated ERP solution that includes the modules and functionality defined in the Requirements document.
The replacement ERP solution is to be implemented in phases or as recommended by the selected vendor and approved by the City.
matches.reason: No candidate states phased implementation or vendor-recommended approach approved by City.

matches.gold_text: Vendors invited to demonstrate their product should be prepared to discuss the application's best practices and its ability to adapt to user preferences.
The City's estimated implementation window runs from March 2025 through January 2027.
All modules in scope must go live by January 1, 2027.
Finalist vendors must follow the City's pre-defined script during their software demonstrations.
The proposal must be one electronic PDF copy, in the order defined in the response format table, not exceeding 100 total pages excluding sample contracts.
The response must include one completed copy of the Requirements document in MS Word format, with the Word format unmodified.
Proposals should be emailed to the City contact at Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov.
All data, materials and documentation originated and prepared for the City under this solicitation belong to the City.
Vendor questions about the RFP may be submitted by email to the City contact by August 28, 2024, 3:00 p.m. PT.
matches.reason: Same deadline: August 28, 2024, 3:00 p.m. PT for questions.

matches.gold_text: Vendor responses should include the sections outlined in the Proposal Response Format; deviation may lead to the response being deemed non-responsive and disqualified.
Marketing literature should not be included in the proposal.
The proposal must begin with a cover letter that is an executive summary of the proposed software and services, limited to two pages.
The vendor must complete the Pricing Summary from Exhibit A, indicating costs for software and implementation services.
Pricing must be comprehensive, including all taxes and available discounts.
Pricing must remain valid for 180 days from the response date.
The vendor must price the software for the user counts defined in the RFP.
The vendor must provide a separate pricing sheet for each deployment option offered (SaaS or on-premises).
Implementation pricing must include all costs required for go-live, including software deployment, data conversion, system configuration, report development, testing and training.
The vendor must price ongoing license and maintenance for Years 1-10.
Financials software must be priced for 130 named users and 85 concurrent users.
Human Capital Management software must be priced for 400 FTEs and 744 W2s.

The proposal must include an implementation overview covering methodology, sample project plan, City and vendor resources, process improvement, change management, data conversion, testing, training and report development.
matches.reason: Implementation overview elements: methodology, plan, resources, change, conversion, testing, training, reports.

matches.gold_text: The proposal must include an overview of support services offered, including hours, response times, support tiers, post go-live services, backup and disaster recovery.
matches.reason: Support overview: hours, response times, post go-live, backup, disaster recovery.

matches.gold_text: The proposal must include a technology overview covering architecture and deployment options, data centers, hardware, mobile, remote access, integration tools and software updates.
matches.reason: Technology overview: architecture, deployment, data centers, hardware, mobile, remote, integration, updates.

matches.gold_text: The proposal must include a security overview covering the security model, standards, SSO/SAML administration, multi-factor authentication and breach response.
matches.reason: Security overview: model, standards, SSO/SAML, MFA, breach response.

matches.gold_text: The vendor must provide references from three current and two prior customers for the proposed software, using the Exhibit B forms.
matches.reason: Exhibit B references with three current customers; prior customers count missing.

matches.gold_text: Preference is for references from Washington State public sector clients.
The vendor must disclose any contract terminations or legal actions with customers in the past five years, describing each situation with the contracting party's name and address.
The proposal must include sample contract documents such as a statement of work, license agreement, maintenance or support agreements and service level agreements.
The vendor must document any exceptions it has to the RFP content.
The vendor's Requirements responses will be incorporated into the signed contract.
matches.reason: No candidate states that Requirements responses are incorporated into the signed contract.

matches.gold_text: The vendor must provide a rating and a comment for every item in the Requirements document; blank responses may cause rejection.
matches.reason: R052 requires a rating and comment per item; R108 states blank responses may cause rejection.

matches.gold_text: The vendor must not include hyperlinks in the Requirements document.
The vendor must not modify the format, font or numbering of the Requirements section or insert page breaks.
Requirement comments must give a substantive explanation; generic comments such as "Standard Functionality" are unacceptable.
Each line-item response in the Requirements document must be limited to 100 words.
The vendor must provide a certification of insurance before commencing any work.
An underwriter's endorsement with additional insured verbiage is required, and the surety must be admitted in the State of Washington.

component_records.title: Programme mobilisation, methodology and schedule
component_records.description: Delivers a defined and proven implementation methodology, adapted from the vendor's standard ERP delivery method, with a sample project plan showing phases, tasks, dependencies and dates across the March 2025 to January 2027 window. Sets the phased structure with a readiness phase, a build and configure phase and a staged go-live, and commits all modules in scope to go live by January 1, 2027. Staffs the programme with named vendor roles, responsibilities and average time per month, and sets out the City roles and time commitments the City must supply. Confirms availability for the December 2024 software demos, the January 2025 due diligence review and contract negotiations from January 2025 onward, and runs the on-site demo strictly to the City's pre-defined script, demonstrating each functional and technical requirement the script calls for. Provides additional information, interviews and follow-up demonstrations on request. Reports progress monthly to the City's executive sponsor against the baseline plan.

component_records.title: Financials module configuration
component_records.description: Configures the eight required financial modules: General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Capital Assets and Enterprise Cashiering. Each module is configured to the vendor's standard best practice rather than a rebuild of the City's current processes, with fit-gap workshops per module and a documented decision log. Delivers the integrated ERP scope defined in the City's Requirements document, with every line item rated and commented in the City's own template. Implements transaction logging that stamps every transaction with user, date, time and before and after values, and builds the audit history report the City can run to review that log. Sizes the configuration to the City's stated financials environment of 130 named and 85 concurrent users.

component_records.title: Human Capital Management configuration and ERP integration
component_records.description: Configures the Human Resources, Time and Attendance and Payroll modules for 400 FTEs and 744 W2s, either as part of the integrated suite or as a best-of-breed HCM product where that scores better against the City's Requirements document. Where a best-of-breed HCM product is proposed, delivers and tests the integration to the selected ERP system for employee master data, position and costing data, payroll journal entries and time-to-payroll flows, using the vendor's published integration tools and APIs. Demonstrates the integration tools and methodology offered, including file-based and API patterns, error handling and reconciliation controls. Documents the integration architecture so the City can see which system is master for each data domain.

component_records.title: Data conversion and report development
component_records.description: Runs a data conversion workstream with a documented methodology covering extraction, profiling, cleansing, mapping, mock loads, reconciliation and sign-off, and a recommended conversion scope by module stating the years of history, data elements and volumes to be converted. Builds the City's reports and dashboards on the new platform, replacing the reports currently produced from the legacy systems, with a report inventory agreed per module and a development, review and acceptance cycle. Prices data conversion and report development as separate implementation service lines with stated assumptions. Converts open balances, active contracts, capital assets and employee records so that go-live is not dependent on parallel running of legacy systems.

component_records.title: Testing, training and change management
component_records.description: Delivers a testing methodology and toolset covering unit, integration, security, performance, user acceptance and regression testing, with entry and exit criteria per cycle and defect tracking reported to the City. Delivers a training methodology and tools including role-based curricula, train-the-trainer for City super users, sandbox environments and quick reference guides, plus a business change management methodology with a stakeholder and communications plan and a process improvement strategy that moves the City onto the vendor's best practices. Prices training as its own implementation service line with stated assumptions. Hands over a trained user base and a support model before each go-live wave.

component_records.title: Technical platform, hosting and security
component_records.description: Delivers the technical platform in the deployment option the City selects, with a separate priced sheet for SaaS and for on-premises so the City can compare both. Confirms the platform, database and accessibility position against the City's IT strategy, including WCAG conformance for the browser-based screens. Provides the integration tools and methodology used across the estate, and states the software update schedule, whether updates are scheduled or automatic, and the update window. Documents the security model, the security standards met, SSO and SAML administration, multi-factor authentication, and breach handling covering customer communication, response and cost. States the data centre locations and redundancy, hardware specifications for the on-premises option, mobile hardware and operating system support, and remote access capabilities.

component_records.title: Support, hosting operations and disaster recovery
component_records.description: Provides support services with stated hours of cover, guaranteed response times by severity, the resources assigned and the escalation path to named managers. Compares baseline support against premium support so the City can choose the level it is buying, and describes the user groups and conferences available to City staff. Delivers the backup strategy and its support arrangements, and disaster recovery covering backup frequency, redundancy and recovery location, again distinguishing baseline from premium. Sets out post go-live tools and services including a hypercare period, a managed service desk and release management for the first year after each go-live wave.

component_records.title: Commercial, pricing and compliance workstream
component_records.description: Completes the City's Pricing Summary in Exhibit A as the priced response, with software and implementation services costs, all taxes and available discounts included, and prices held valid for 180 days from the response date. States Year 1 software cost with the bidder's assumptions, prices implementation services across Implementation, Data Conversion, Training, Report Development, Integration, Travel and Other each with assumptions, and states subscription or maintenance separately for each of Years 2 through 10. Shows the Software, Implementation and Maintenance/License sub-totals and the Total, and prices the financial and HCM module sets against the City's stated user counts. Adds a separate pricing sheet per deployment option and an estimated modification cost for every requirement rated 2. Carries the City's terms and conditions as the basis of the proposal, acknowledges the RFP and its exhibits, and confirms the City's ownership of all data, materials and documentation. Provides the certification of insurance before any work starts, evidenced by an underwriter's endorsement with additional insured wording and an admitted surety in Washington State, and confirms the vendor bears its own bid costs and accepts the risk allocation for RFP errors it failed to notify. Runs the clarification process, submitting the vendor's written questions to the City by the August 28, 2024 3:00 p.m. PT deadline and incorporating the City's September 5, 2024 answers into the priced and technical response.

component_records.title: Requirements response and reference evidence
component_records.description: Completes the City's ERP Requirements document in its original Word format, rating every line item on the City's 4/3/2/0/F scale with a specific comment on how the software meets the function, no blank rows, no hyperlinks and no cross-references, and each response within the 100-word limit. Names the third-party application for every item rated 3 and the anticipated release month and year for every item rated F. Supplies three current and two prior customer references on the City's forms, prioritising Washington State public sector clients of comparable size and scope, and discloses any contract terminated in the past five years and any legal action with a customer, naming the contracting party. Presents the vendor's organisational strength, financial viability and product vision, and its record of implementing ERP for government entities, including cities of similar size and service scope.

items.text: All modules must be live by January 1, 2027 on a fixed 22-month window. The City scores Implementation at 25 points and requires every financial and HCM module live by January 1, 2027, inside a March 2025 to January 2027 window with no milestones defined. If any module slips, the bidder loses evaluation points and, after award, misses a contractual date that the City has made a scored commitment. Eleven modules plus data conversion, integration, reports and training in 22 months is tight for a city of this size, and the RFP sets no intermediate milestones, so the risk turns on phasing the City has not yet approved.
items.reason: Dates, 25 points and go-live are supported; 'eleven modules' and 'every financial and HCM module' not stated; 22-month and no-milestones are inferred.

items.text: Best-of-breed HCM integration target is undefined. The City will accept a best-of-breed HCM product that integrates with the selected ERP, but the ERP is not yet chosen, so the interfaces for employee master data, position and costing data and payroll journals have no defined target. If the City selects a different ERP than the one the bidder integrates against, the integration must be rebuilt at the bidder's cost. The integration scope is real work in the price, and the RFP leaves the ERP selection open, so the risk depends on a fact the RFP does not settle.
items.reason: Best-of-breed HCM integration is supported; specific interface data types and bidder bearing rebuild cost are not in sources.

items.text: Scope of the Requirements document is not stated to be exhaustive. The RFP says the Requirements document is not a comprehensive list of the City's requirements, so obligations outside it may still be evaluated or written into the contract. The proposed solution assumes the Requirements document is the complete scope, which leaves the bidder exposed to unpriced work after award. The solution's first assumption treats the Requirements document as complete scope while the RFP says the opposite, and the City also reserves the right to reject proposals that miss required features.
items.reason: Non-comprehensive requirements and possible elimination are supported; solution's assumption and 'reserves right to reject' differ; contract incorporation limited to key requirements.

items.text: Best-practice adoption scope is undefined. The City intends to adopt the vendor's best practices rather than replicate current processes, but the RFP does not say which processes must be re-engineered. If the City expects process change beyond standard configuration of the eleven modules, fit-gap workshops, change management and training effort grow beyond the priced estimate. The solution limits process re-engineering to standard module configuration, while the City's stated intent to change processes is open-ended, so extra effort is expected unless the boundary is agreed.
items.reason: Best-practice intent supported; 'eleven modules', fit-gap workshops and the solution's limit on re-engineering not in cited sources.

items.text: Demo script not issued, so demo preparation is speculative. Finalists must demo on-site strictly to a pre-defined Demo Script that the City issues only with the shortlist notification, and the demo is scored on script adherence and on demonstrated functional coverage. Preparing against an assumed script risks a weak demo score on a criterion worth 30 points for Software and 15 for Technology. The script is not in the RFP and the solution assumes it mirrors the Requirements document, which is itself missing, so preparation rests on two unverified assumptions.
items.reason: Script adherence scoring supported; 'on-site' and script issued with notification are in S8.1; 30/15 points are Software/Technology categories, not demo-specific.

items.text: Pricing basis for maintenance years and deployment options is unsettled. The RFP requires maintenance priced for Years 1 to 10 and a separate pricing sheet per deployment option, but does not say whether Year 1 maintenance is bundled into the software cost or whether both SaaS and on-premises must be priced. Getting this wrong changes the Total on Exhibit A and can make the bid non-compliant or mispriced against competitors. The solution assumes Year 1 maintenance is bundled and that SaaS is primary with on-premises for comparison, both inferences the RFP does not confirm.
items.reason: Years 1-10 maintenance and separate sheets supported; Exhibit A shows Year 1 software and Years 2-10 maintenance; solution assumptions not in sources.

items.text: Insurance limits and City terms are not specified. The bidder must certify insurance with an underwriter's endorsement and an admitted Washington surety, and must accept the City's terms and conditions on pain of rejection, but the RFP states no coverage types, limits or amounts and does not identify the terms document. Insurance priced at the wrong level or a proposal that varies the City's terms can be rejected or cost more than budgeted. The solution assumes customary municipal limits pending City confirmation, and the RFP's silence on both points means the exposure depends on facts the RFP does not give.
items.reason: Insurance, endorsement, surety, and rejection for other terms are in sources; silence on limits is consistent with them.

items.text: Reference evidence may not meet the City's comparability test. The bidder must supply three current and two prior references on the City's forms, with preference for Washington State public sector clients of similar size and scope, and must disclose any terminated contract or customer legal action in the past five years. If the reference pool is thin or a disclosure is unfavourable, the Vendor criterion worth 15 points is weakened and the proposal may be judged non-responsive. The RFP does not define what makes a reference comparable, and the solution assumes a population and employee-count test the City has not confirmed.
items.reason: Exhibit B has three current customers and two prior; 15 points for Vendor is in S8.1, not cited here; solution assumption unsupported.

items.text: Proposal format and page limit are ambiguous. The RFP states the 100-page limit twice with different wording and refers to a required proposal order in a table that is not in the document, while deviations may be treated as non-responsive. A proposal that exceeds the cap or misorders sections risks disqualification after the bid team has spent the full effort. The solution assumes the cap is hard and that the Word Requirements document sits outside it, which the RFP does not confirm.
items.reason: Page limit appears twice with slightly different wording and the table is missing, but 'Word document sits outside cap' is not stated; solution assumption unsupported.}

items.text: Unreadable page 5 may hide scope or submission instructions. Page 5 of the RFP is dominated by an image that could not be read, and it sits in the early sections that carry the client situation and scope. If it contains environment tables, module lists or submission instructions, the bid team may miss scope or a compliance step. Only one page is affected and its content is unknown, so the impact is material only if it carries scope or instructions the rest of the RFP does not repeat.

Question and proposal deadlines may move under the City's reservation. The City reserves the right to modify or reschedule the timeline, and the RFP gives the question deadline and proposal deadline in more than one place with different wording. A bid team that plans to a moved date, or that misses the August 28, 2024 3:00 p.m. PT question cutoff, loses the chance to fix the scope and pricing ambiguities above. The solution treats both dates as firm, which is the safe reading, but the RFP's reservation and the conflicting references leave a real chance of a change.
items.reason: Reservation and dates are supported, but 'conflicting references' overstates: dates are consistent across sources, differing only in wording; scope and pricing ambiguities not cited.
